<style>
  /* SEEN ON bar — mobile & small screens only */
  @media (max-width: 767px) {

    /* One line, left-aligned, spacing scales with screen width */
    .seen-on {
      display: flex !important;
      flex-wrap: nowrap !important;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: flex-start;
      gap: clamp(6px, 2vw, 16px);
      /* padding shrinks as the content shrinks (top | sides | bottom) */
      padding: clamp(4px, 1.5vw, 10px) 0 clamp(8px, 2.5vw, 16px) !important;
    }

    /* The two inner wrappers (text side + logos side) */
    .seen-on > div {
      display: flex !important;
      flex-wrap: nowrap !important;
      align-items: center;
      min-width: 0;
    }

    /* Gap between the logos */
    .seen-on > div:last-child {
      gap: clamp(4px, 1.5vw, 12px);
    }

    /* Text scales down, never wraps */
    .seen-on > div:first-child div {
      white-space: nowrap;
      font-size: clamp(9px, 2.4vw, 13px);
    }

    /* Logos scale by height, width follows automatically */
    .seen-on img {
      height: clamp(14px, 4vw, 28px) !important;
      width: auto !important;
      max-width: none;
    }
  }
</style>
New smartwatch alternative under £100, with no subscription - on purpose.

Serial founders Topi Joonas and Ryan Scott have built successful businesses together for years. Two friends, two dads, both entrepreneurs with a habit of fixing what annoys them. Now they've built the HLTH Band. And it's selling out across the U.K.

Almost everyone wants to stay on top of their health. But few people are happy with their tracker. Most are bulky. Some are inaccurate. Many die after a day. And the worst of them make you rent your own data with monthly fees.

They wanted to change that.

After 1 year, £200,000 in research and development, with the help of the top engineers in Asia (formerly behind the Amazon Halo) the HLTH band was created.

The result? The first screen-free fitness tracker to deliver continuous blood pressure, sleep, heart rate and HRV tracking using multi-wavelength PPG. With no subscription, all for under £100.
It All Started With Topi's Dad's Cardiac Event

He survived. But it shook the whole family. Staying on top of your health wasn't a someday plan anymore. Now it was everything.

His dad had worn his pricey smartwatch every single day.

But when it came to his actual health, it told him next to nothing. It buzzed with messages. It counted steps. And it died every night. Exactly when it was supposed to be tracking his health.

Ryan's family had a different version of the same problem.

His grandma's GP told her to start tracking her health. But the device he recommended cost over £300. She couldn't afford it. So she never started and just one month later contracted a virus which paralyzed her from the neck down. She also survived, but the damage was already done.

Two families. Same problem. Real health tracking was either a hassle or too expensive. And after becoming first-time dads, the mission was never more clear. Build a tracker they could trust themselves, and that people can actually afford.
It took a year, £200,000, and six trips to meet the engineers in person

Topi and Ryan didn't outsource. They went directly to the factories behind the world's biggest wearable brands. They found the same chip suppliers, the engineering talent, and the data scientists they needed for the mission.

They lost count of how many prototypes they went through.

But all of it led to exactly what they set out to build.

Accurate, lightweight, comfortable, and waterproof, so it never comes off. No screen to distract you and 30 days on a single charge. A truly affordable dedicated fitness tracker.

But the business model is most surprising in a time the kids on TikTok call "Subscription Hell."

But releasing at a fair price with no subscription was a deliberate choice, say the founders.

"We could have charged a monthly fee," Topi says. "Everyone else does. But the people who need this most are exactly the ones who shouldn't have to keep paying just to see their own health data."
Why the data is actually different

A smartwatch spreads its power across a bright screen, apps, and constant notifications.

The HLTH Band has no screen. So nearly all its power goes to one job: the sensors. That means it reads your body far more often than a watch ever could. Tracking blood pressure, heart rate, HRV, and sleep using the same multi-wavelength light sensors found in GP clinics.

More readings, taken more consistently, build a clearer picture of your health over time. With most trackers, you're never quite sure the numbers are real. That doubt sits quietly in the back of your mind. But the HLTH Band reads steadily, day after day, so you can finally trust what you see.
"I wish I'd had this years ago"

As of April 2026, hlthtrack.com released in the U.K. and sold out three times. So the team at HLTH has partnered with the same chip suppliers behind the world's biggest wearable brands to keep it available across the U.K.

Now, Brits everywhere can experience effortless health tracking and accurate data for an affordable price. All with a device so comfortable, you'll completely forget you're wearing it.

The founder Topi says, "You can change what you measure. The HLTH Band is your chance to take control, with just one small step."

[Update [16/06/2026]: The ongoing global chip shortage is affecting supply across the wearable technology sector. HLTH has confirmed stock is limited and a price increase is scheduled for the coming weeks. If you're considering it, now is the time.]
